risks.risk: You may be buying a PS5 game case, not a PS5 console (seller’s wording suggests console, but photo shows only the game).
risks.proof: Ask for a photo showing the actual PS5 console (front + back ports) and the box/serial label.

risks.risk: If it is a console, it could be disc vs digital edition, which affects value.
risks.proof: Photo of the console model/label and a shot of the disc drive area (or confirmation it’s digital).
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lower-value worst case (disc edition uncertainty treated as not confirmed).

risks.risk: Condition/working status (overheating, ports, controller pairing) can’t be verified from a single game cover photo.
risks.proof: Short video showing power-on, game load, controller connection, and a quick ports check (HDMI/USB).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst case: needs repair/has faults).

risks.risk: Accessories may be incomplete (controller, cables, stand, original pads) and receipt may not be included.
risks.proof: Photo laid out showing every included item + receipt/serial match if available.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming missing accessories (worst case: only the item shown).

proof_requests: Send photos of the actual PS5 console: front, back ports, and the serial/model label.
Send a photo showing whether it’s disc or digital edition.
Send a short video: console boots to home screen, controller connects, and one game loads.
Send a full accessories layout photo (controller(s), cables, stand, and any “pads”) plus the UK receipt.
response.reason: The only photo shows a God of War Ragnarök PS5 game case, while the seller claims a neatly used PS5 console with working ports and accessories. Without console photos/tests, a correct worst-case price can’t be set confidently.
